artifacts.summary: 6-phase plan generalizing deploy-headless.sh's own function-wrap self-overwrite mitigation to both genuine deploy-caller sites, plus a red-first regression test, a mechanical class-guard lint, and two doc corrections.

memory_candidates.content: Bash reads a running script incrementally by byte offset, so any deployed script that triggers a redeploy overwriting its own file has its remaining top-level statements corrupted mid-execution (silent truncation, or a spurious error such as 'unbound variable' pointing at a line that contains no such variable). The mitigation that works deterministically is structural, not path-based: wrap the invocation and ALL code textually after it -- through true EOF -- in a single function defined before it runs and invoked as the file's last physical statement, so the whole body is parsed before any overwrite can occur. A partial wrap merely relocates the hazard to the first top-level statement after the closing brace. Switching WHICH copy of the deploying script is invoked (source store vs deployed) does not help: the victim is the caller, not the deployer.
